gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-ends-with: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-ends-with: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-ends-with: Section '`Class::method` Is Static or Unbound...': 'With more parameters, the first becomes the receiver and the rest the arguments: as a Comparator<String>, compare(a, b) calls a.compareToIgnoreCase(b).' So apply("ledger-q3.csv", ".csv") calls "ledger-q3.csv".endsWith(".csv"), which is true. (The page does not state that String has no static endsWith; the option relies on the method name's ordinary meaning.)
recorded.prompt:q-double-to-string: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-double-to-string: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-double-to-string: Same section: 'When both searches find one, it does not pick', with the javac error 'reference to toString is ambiguous / both method toString(int) in Integer and method toString() in Integer match'; 'Integer has a static toString(int) that takes the Integer by unboxing'; 'Long::toString and Integer::hashCode fail the same way.' With the stem's fact that Double declares both, the reader concludes Double::toString is ambiguous by direct analogy. Double itself is not named on the page; the conclusion is by analogy with Integer/Long.

recorded.pass:q-port-queues: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-port-queues: Section '`Class::new` Picks Its Constructor...': 'computeIfAbsent takes a Function<? super K, ? extends V> and calls it with the key. With Integer keys, ArrayList::new resolves to ArrayList(int initialCapacity)'; 'sized.apply(5) is an empty list with room for five elements, not a list holding 5' (output '[] [] size=0'); 'Capacities 3 and 1 are legal'. So 8080 gives an empty list, add(17) makes it [17]. The page says negative capacities throw and 40,000,000 ran out of memory with -Xmx64m; 8080 is plainly a legal small positive capacity.
